conflict_topics: ventilation responsibility (who must ventilate when cooking)
moving Agent C's drying rack / consent to move shared items
dialogue_quality_notes: Agents present concrete proposals and conditions (trial period, cost-splitting, wattage check) rather than circular demands.
Agent A softens immediate stance (agrees to extractor now) while resisting blanket rule; this is a natural compromise sequence.
Agent C's consent is conditional on receiving the cost estimate; interdependencies are clearly signalled.
Agent D acts primarily as a time-sensitive requester for stove access and accepts a short wait.
evaluation.final_reason: By the end of the run immediate practical disputes were mostly narrowed: Agent A agreed to run the extractor now and free the stove in two minutes; Agent B agreed not to move Agent C's drying rack without permission and will provide an electricity estimate. However the substantive dispute over adopting a blanket rule assigning ventilation duty to the cook and the agreed method/amount for splitting extra electricity remains unresolved pending the cost estimate and a joint decision, so the overall situation is only partially resolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A: softened position on immediate action (agreed to run extractor now and for 10 minutes after; agreed to free stove in two minutes) but retained opposition to a pre-imposed blanket rule. Evidence: R2 Turn 3 and R6 Turn 14.

Agent B: initially insisted cook should ventilate and proposed a rule; then offered concrete cost-splitting and agreed not to move Agent C's rack, and committed to measure extractor wattage. Evidence: R1 Turn 2, R2 Turn 4, R3 Turn 6.
Agent C: moved from silence at the opening to conditional agreement to the one-month trial contingent on a cost estimate and preservation of their drying rack. Evidence: R3 Turn 5, R4 Turn 7.
Agent D: consistently requested timely stove access and accepted waiting until Agent A frees the stove; no major position change beyond waiting. Evidence: R4-R6 Turns 8,10,13.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A refuses a blanket rule and refuses the immediate two-minute stop, offering mitigation measures instead: "I won't agree to a rule that always puts ventilation duty on the cook." Agent B insists the cook must ventilate and proposes the rule: "whoever cooks turns the extractor on while cooking and leaves it on for 10 minutes afterwards." The incompatible claims about blanket responsibility remain.

Agent A concedes to leave the extractor on now and for 10 minutes after tonight but rejects accepting that as a blanket rule without a fair sharing plan: "I'll leave the extractor on now and for 10 minutes after I'm done. I won't accept that as a blanket rule unless we agree a fair sharing plan." Agent B refines the proposal with a cost-split and trial. Immediate odour control is agreed, but the future rule remains contested.

Agent C conditionally accepts a one-month trial but adds conditions: don't move my drying rack without asking, and provide an estimate of extra electricity. Agent B agrees not to move the rack without asking and offers to measure or check wattage for an estimate. The main outstanding item is the cost estimate and formalising the rule; direct opposition is reduced.

Agent C reiterates they will agree once they see the estimate. Agent D presses for stove access: "Agent A — how long until your stove's free?" The unresolved issues now include the pending cost estimate/future rule and stove access timing; no new settlement is reached.

Agent B commits to check the extractor rating and return with a monthly extra-cost estimate in five minutes. Agent D repeats the request about the stove and agrees to wait. Progress is made toward resolving the cost-information gap, but substantive issues (future rule/cost split and stove timing) remain unsettled.

Agent A gives a short, practical accommodation for stove access: "Two minutes. I'll lower the heat and put a lid on and leave the extractor on. I'll ping you when the stove's free." The immediate stove-access conflict is resolved; outstanding substantive disagreement is limited to the future blanket rule and the as-yet-unproduced cost estimate.

substantive_insights: The core tension is between immediate odour control/practical convenience and fairness in distributing ongoing burdens (electricity cost and responsibility).
Agents move toward evidence-based resolution: agreeing a time-limited trial and requesting a measured electricity estimate rather than guessing costs.
Consent over moving personal items (Agent C's drying rack) is a distinct constraint that shapes feasible ventilation actions; respecting that consent was accepted verbally by Agent B.
